note: Lateness signal: firms that delay earnings relative to own historical average. Livnat-Zhang (SSRN 2497115) + Chambers-Penman (1984 JAR): late announcers have negative news / earnings management. Signal = days since last quarterly EPS vs 5yr own-mean = cross-section of lateness. SHORT firms that delay relative to own history (bad news delay). field verified via lessons-learned: days_from_last_change(actual_eps_value_quarterly) used in recency-weighting rnd 33. Fallback: ts_delta(days_from_last_change(actual_eps_value_quarterly), 252) = trend in announcement speed. INTERPOLATION candidate: corr unknown, suggest ts_rank construction first.

AR-growth vs Sales-growth divergence = channel stuffing / revenue pull-forward proxy. Lewellen-Resutek (2016 RAS 21:4): receivable accrual component gives -0.71%/month long-short. Thomas-Zhang (2002): receivable changes = strongest accrual component. SHORT firms where AR grows faster than sales. fields: receivable, sales both standard pv1/fnd6. CAUTION: DSO-level used in #28 (group_rank DSO x close-range) and #16 (@TOP500 DSO leg); this is DELTA of DSO ratio = different from level -- probe as ts_rank construction: ts_rank(-ts_delta(receivable/(sales+1),63), 252) as alternative.

5yr ROA volatility = earnings PREDICTABILITY factor. Dichev-Tang (2009 JAE 47): earnings predictability (low ROA variance) predicts returns and P/E ratios. Firms with stable ROA outperform (less parameter uncertainty). SHORT high-variance = unpredictable earnings. DISTINCT from accrual-quality-variance (#48, Wjg2gbEo) which uses ts_std_dev((op_income-CFO)/assets, 1260) -- the ACCRUAL COMPONENT variance, not ROA variance itself. fields: op_income, assets standard verified. CAUTION: lessons say vol-of-fundamental closed except sales-vol (vRmZZalG); Huang/Francis CFO-vol flat (-0.07) rnd46 -- but ROA-vol = different base than CFO-vol. RISK: may correlate with accrual-quality #48 (0.87 mention). Flag for translator to check self-corr vs Wjg2gbEo.

Trend in announcement speed: firms increasingly reporting FASTER = positive signal (good news acceleration). ts_delta of days-since-last-quarterly-EPS over 1yr = trend in timeliness. Livnat-Zhang (SSRN 2497115): firms that advance announcements have positive surprises. SHORT firms where reporting lag is increasing (slowing = bad news accumulation). DISTINCT from earn-timing-delay (level of lateness vs own mean) -- this is TREND in reporting speed = trajectory. Chambers-Penman (1984): announcement speed trajectory contains news content. INTERPOLATION candidate or standalone group_rank. UNVERIFIED nuance: ts_delta of days_from_last_change may produce sparse data -- translator should verify behavior.
